segments.text: A mother prayed for a hundred years for a son who would kill the king of the gods. With three days left, Indra did something terrible and cut the unborn child apart. What he cut could not be killed. So how did Indra survive? The mother was Diti. Vishnu had killed her sons Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu. She asked her husband, the sage Kashyapa, for a son who would kill Indra. Kashyapa gave strict rules: live a pure life for a hundred years, never lie down without washing your feet. If she failed, her son would be Indra's friend. Indra hid near her hut, waiting for one mistake. There was none. Her prayers kept her womb safe like a fort. Her belly grew. His end came closer. Then, three days before the birth, Diti was so tired that she fell asleep without washing her feet. Indra jumped. He went into her womb. His Vajra, his thunder weapon, flashed. Seven pieces. Then he stopped. The pieces were alive. They cried. "Maruda!" he shouted. "Don't cry!" They only cried louder. He cut each piece into seven more. Still alive, still louder. Diti woke up. Indra ran away. She gave birth to 49 children. They did not kill Indra. They became his friends, as Kashyapa had said. Because Indra shouted, "Maruda," they were called the Marutas, the storm gods. That is how Indra survived. Diti's son could not be killed, only made into many, and all 49 stood beside him.
